title: The Fox and the Snake
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Snake, in crossing a river, was carried away by the current, but managed to wriggle on to a bundle of thorns which was floating by, and was thus carried at a great rate down-stream. A Fox caught sight of it from the bank as it went whirling along, and called out, "Gad! the passenger fits the ship!"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Snake doing when it was carried away?
According to the passage, what did the Snake manage to wriggle onto?
According to the passage, how was the Snake carried once it was on the thorns?
According to the passage, from where did the Fox see the Snake?
According to the passage, what exact words does the Fox call out?
As the passage uses it, what does "wriggle" mean in "managed to wriggle on to a bundle of thorns"?
options: To twist and squirm its way
To swim in a straight line

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Fox mean by "the passenger fits the ship"?
options: That the Snake is too heavy for the thorns to carry
That the prickly, unpleasant raft suits the unpleasant creature riding on it
That the Snake built the raft of thorns itself
That the thorns will sink under the Snake's weight

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Two disagreeable things can turn out to be perfectly matched to each other
Snakes are more clever than foxes in a crisis
Rivers are always dangerous to cross
Thorns should never be trusted to float

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what carried the Snake away in the first place?
According to the passage, what was the bundle of thorns doing in the river?
According to the passage, how does the Fox describe the way the Snake and thorns went along the water?
As the passage uses it, what does "current" mean in "was carried away by the current"?
options: The flowing movement of the river's water
A type of small dried fruit

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is the Fox's remark meant as a joke rather than a compliment?
options: It points out that a prickly, unwelcome raft is a fitting match for a creature many find unpleasant
It suggests the Snake actually enjoys being carried by the current
It praises the Snake's cleverness in finding the thorns
It warns the Snake that the thorns will soon sink

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Snake escapes a river current by climbing onto floating thorns, and a watching Fox jokes that the odd pair suit each other
A Fox rescues a drowning Snake from a river
A Snake and a Fox race each other down a river
A Fox warns a Snake to avoid a bundle of thorns
